topics.topic: Authoritative source and completeness guarantees for replaying post-backup erasures
questions: What authoritative record tells the owner which customer or project erasures to repeat, and what happens if that record is absent or incomplete?
What authoritative record enumerates all customer, project and audit-log erasures after the backup, and how is completeness verified before serving resumes?
What durable source and replay semantics guarantee that every post-backup erasure is reapplied correctly before service resumes?

quotes: After restoring production from a backup, the owner repeats every erasure made after the backup's instant, as the owner's retention review recorded it (R0-60), before the instance serves again.

The audit log's period is the governance's. In the periodic review the owner erases, confirming, every entry older than a date the owner gives; that erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date.
judgement.divergence: One implementation blocks serving until a complete external erasure ledger is verified and replays every recorded erasure; another trusts whatever records are available and may serve restored personal data, which the owner and affected customers notice.
judgement.why: The required source, completeness check, and replay behavior for post-backup erasures are not defined.

topics.topic: Cabinet Kernel authority to end an agent session
questions: Is ending an agent session an operation allowed by Cabinet Kernel's token?
Is ending a session an operation allowed to the Cabinet Kernel token?
Is Cabinet Kernel authorized to end an agent session, despite that operation being absent from its A09 rights row?

quotes: | Cabinet Kernel | with agent authority only (A10): register an agent session; read the session's access; request access to a project; validate a project reference; read the agent projection; list rooms; add a room; list artifacts; read the latest artifact of a type; publish and withdraw an artifact pointer (R0-88) | `business_confidential` (R0-74) |
An operation outside a token's row is refused, whatever the request holds.
Cabinet Kernel ends a session when its agent session ends; the owner may end any session in the owner interface.
judgement.why: A09 refuses operations absent from Kernel's row, while A11 requires Kernel to perform the absent end-session operation.

topics.topic: Calendar and time zone defining today for audit erasure
questions: Is “today” also the UTC calendar date or the owner's Europe/Madrid calendar date?
Which calendar and time zone determine whether the supplied date is later than today?
Is 'today' the current UTC date or the owner's local date?

quotes: The date of an erasure is a date not later than today; a later date is refused. Every entry whose instant is before the start of that date (UTC) is removed.
judgement.divergence: One implementation evaluates today in UTC and another in Europe/Madrid; near midnight they accept or refuse the same date differently, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The removal boundary is UTC, but the calendar used to determine today is unspecified.

topics.topic: Classification and production-data safeguards of a restore-test instance
questions: What kind of instance may receive the production backup for the restore test?
What kind of instance is the temporary restore target, and under which production-data guarantees may it hold the restored personal data?
Is the temporary restore instance an allowed exception to the rule that test instances receive no production data?

quotes: Before each release the owner restores the latest backup into a temporary instance on VM Platform, checks that it starts (A17) and answers, and removes it; a test instance never receives a production backup (R0-34).

Each holds its own identity space and no production
personal data; nothing moves between an instance and production except by an
explicit import (R0-34).
judgement.why: The required temporary non-production restore receives production data despite the categorical rule that every other instance holds none.

topics.topic: Concurrency semantics for publishing and withdrawing a pointer
questions: What outcome is required when a publish and a withdrawal of the currently published pointer occur concurrently?
How are these operations linearized, and which operations are accepted or refused for each possible race?
What outcomes are allowed when publication and withdrawal of the same project's type occur concurrently?

quotes: Publishes of one type on one project are serialised: of two concurrent ones, each sees the other's result, and both are accepted with consecutive versions.
Withdrawing marks the pointer `withdrawn` with its instant and principal in one transaction; it never makes an earlier version `published` (R0-14).
judgement.divergence: One implementation linearizes withdrawal first and then publishes a new current version; another publishes first and then withdraws or refuses the withdrawal, producing different pointer histories visible to callers.
judgement.why: Publication is serialized only against publication, leaving publication-versus-withdrawal and withdrawal-versus-withdrawal races undefined.

topics.topic: Confirmation binding, lifetime, consumption, storage, and retry semantics
questions: Is a confirmation consumed by the first attempt or only by an accepted change, when does an unused confirmation expire, and may it be retried after a stale revision or import conflict?

What value proves the pre-action confirmation, what exact action, target, revision and inputs is it bound to, where is its one-use state kept, and is that value distinct from the confirmation id written after acceptance?
Until when is a shown confirmation valid, and what invalidates or consumes it?

quotes: A confirmation step (Identity formats) is valid only in the session that showed it, and once.

It keeps no Confirmation record; how the owner interface carries the
confirmation step belongs to States 2 and 5.

A confirmation id is minted only for an accepted, confirmed action that changes state, and is written into its entry (and, for the import, into the migration closure); a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none.
judgement.divergence: One implementation consumes a short-lived confirmation on the first attempt and binds it to exact inputs; another keeps it usable until an accepted change and permits retry after failure, which changes what the owner can execute.
judgement.why: The texts do not define the pre-action confirmation value, its binding, expiry, storage, or consumption point.

topics.topic: Current authorization and domain preconditions checked before recognizing a create replay
questions: Before returning a replay, which current preconditions are rechecked for project, Customer and room creates—for example an archived room's project or a now restricted, ended or erased linked Customer?
For project, Customer and room creates, which current authorization and parent/customer-state checks run before replay recognition?
Does a valid replay return its existing record before current parent and domain preconditions are checked, such as an add-room replay after its project was archived?

quotes: A create whose request id an existing record of the same model already carries, with the same supplied facts, is a repeat: Registry answers that record as it stands now — archived included — and changes nothing.
The checks of the call come first: a repeat on a project no longer in the session's set or since archived is refused as any call (A10, A07).
judgement.divergence: One implementation recognizes project, Customer, and room replays before current domain checks and returns the existing record; another first refuses a replay whose parent is archived or whose linked Customer is now ineligible, which callers notice.
judgement.why: Only publication explicitly orders current authorization and lifecycle checks before replay recognition.

topics.topic: Daily backup cadence, failure handling, retention boundary, and deletion timing
questions: What is a day and a backup's age, when is deletion performed, what happens after a missed or failed backup, and may Registry continue serving without a successful recent backup?
What exact condition satisfies the daily-backup rule, and what must happen when a backup is missed or fails?
Is the limit exactly 30 times 24 hours, 30 calendar days, or a daily cleanup that can retain a backup beyond 30 days, and when is deletion required to run?
What exact cadence and deletion rule satisfy the daily and 30-day requirements?

quotes: Once a day the store is backed up as a consistent copy taken while Registry runs; a backup never holds part of a transaction.

Each backup is encrypted with a key the owner holds in the vault (R0-23), and is kept 30 days; older backups are deleted. An erasure in Registry reaches the backups when the last backup holding the erased values is deleted, at most 30 days after it.
age(oldest backup) <= 30 days
judgement.divergence: One installation enforces a maximum 24-hour interval, retries failures, and deletes at an exact 30-day deadline; another uses calendar-day jobs, continues after missed backups, and cleans up later, which the owner notices in recovery coverage and retention.
judgement.why: The daily cadence, failure response, and precise retention boundary are not operationally defined.

topics.topic: Durable original facts used to compare create-request replays after later edits
questions: Are replay facts compared with the original creation facts or with the record's current editable facts, and where are original facts retained if that is the intended comparison?
Against what durable value is a replay compared after the project or Customer has been corrected, and where is that original value stored?
Against which values is a replay compared after the created record has changed?

quotes: A create whose request id an existing record of the same model already carries, with the same supplied facts, is a repeat: Registry answers that record as it stands now — archived included — and changes nothing.
The supplied facts are compared as the caller gave them, value for value; Registry does not normalise them for the comparison. For 'add a room' the project is one of them.

  anonymised mark (R0-62, R0-87).
judgement.divergence: One implementation compares a replay with immutable original creation facts retained separately; another compares it with the record's current corrected facts, so the same retry is accepted by one and refused by the other, which the caller notices.
judgement.why: Replay comparison requires original supplied facts, but the model records only the request id and mutable current facts.

topics.topic: History and pointer semantics when a removed artifact type is reintroduced
questions: May a later release re-declare a removed type, and if so do its old pointers and version sequence become active history for new publishes and withdrawals?
May the same type be re-added, and if so do new versions continue after the old maximum, does its former published pointer become the current pointer again, and may old pointers be withdrawn?
Does re-adding the same type resume its existing version history and published pointer, or create a logically new vocabulary entry?

quotes: A release that removes a type keeps every pointer of it: they stay in the history and are listed and read as before, with their status as it was.
After the removal, publishing that type and 'read the latest artifact of a type' for it are refused as an unknown type, and withdrawing a pointer of it is refused.
A type never changes its owner service; a move is a removal and a new type.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits re-declaration and resumes the old version sequence and published pointer; another treats the reintroduced name as a fresh type or forbids reintroduction, producing different publish, latest-read, and withdrawal behavior visible to callers.
judgement.why: Removal is defined, but later re-declaration of the same type name is not.

topics.topic: No-op versus refusal when repeating a grant or activation for an archived project
questions: If a project is already granted or active and is then archived, is repeating that grant or activation accepted as a no-op or refused because archived projects cannot be granted or made active?
If an archived project is already granted and the owner grants it again, is the call an accepted no-op or refused because archived-project validation comes first?
What happens when the owner selects as active the same project that remained active after being archived?
If an archived project is already granted or active, is repeating that grant or activation accepted as a no-op or refused because the project is archived?

quotes: A transition to the state a record is already in is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project already in a session's set, making the active project active again, clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered session (R0-53).
Making an archived project active is refused, as granting one is; a project archived while active stays active, and agent writes on it are refused (R0-12).
judgement.why: A05 accepts repeated grants and activation unconditionally, while R0-70 refuses granting or activating an archived project that may already remain granted or active.

topics.topic: Project resolution and authorization for pointer-based operations
questions: For an operation such as withdrawing a pointer, is the checked project derived from the pointer, required explicitly in the request, or taken from the active project when no project id is supplied?

When Kernel withdraws a pointer, must the request also name a project, or must Registry resolve the pointer's project before applying the session-set check, and what is returned when either the pointer or its project is outside the set?
How is the session's project-set check performed for withdrawal or another operation whose direct identifier is a pointer rather than a project?

quotes: A call with agent authority is accepted only when the token is Cabinet Kernel's, the session it names is registered, and — for an operation on a project — the project is in that session's set (R0-46, R0-53).
An operation on a project that names none uses the session's active project; with none active it is refused (R0-69).
A pointer is published and withdrawn by Cabinet Kernel for the agent, on a project of its session's set (R0-46, A10), or by the owner (R0-88).
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires an explicit project id and checks it before resolving the pointer; another derives the project from the pointer or falls back to the active project, producing different authorization and not-found behavior visible to Kernel.
judgement.why: The texts require a project-set check for withdrawal without defining how that project is selected or resolved.

topics.topic: Release dependency boundary and the artifacts whose digests are verified
questions: Does this include transitive packages, the language runtime, native libraries, operating-system packages, database engine, browser assets and build-only tools, or only direct application packages?
What is the closed dependency boundary, and which exact artifact is hashed and verified for each dependency?
What artifacts are members of release.dependencies?

quotes: A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with its digest; a running instance uses exactly those.
Registry has no dependency that loads code at run time from outside its release.
running dependencies = release.dependencies (name, version, digest)
judgement.divergence: One release includes and verifies transitive packages, runtimes, native libraries, and the database engine; another lists only direct application packages, so different unverified code can run and is noticed by release verification and operators.
judgement.why: The closed boundary of runtime dependencies and the artifact represented by each digest are unspecified.

topics.topic: Requests that refresh the owner-session inactivity deadline
questions: Which requests reset the 30-minute idle timer: successful authenticated reads, successful changes, confirmations, refused requests, or any request carrying the session?
Exactly which requests refresh the owner session's inactivity deadline?
Which requests refresh the owner session's inactivity deadline?

quotes: The session ends at the first of: 8 hours after sign-in; 30 minutes without an owner action; the owner's sign-out; the instance's restart (M11 is never durable).

owner_session s valid at t <=> t < s.began + 8h and
                                t < s.last_action + 30min and
                                not signed_out(s) and no restart since s.began
judgement.divergence: One implementation refreshes inactivity on every authenticated owner request, including reads and refusals; another refreshes only on accepted changes, causing the owner to be signed out at different times.
judgement.why: Owner action and the update rule for last_action are not defined.

topics.topic: Required new-Customer mapping inputs and confirmation during import
questions: Must the mapping display and require confirmation of the new Customer's name, kind, tax-id decision and discarded legacy value, and what validation refuses confirmation when any is missing?
Must the preview collect and show each new Customer's name, kind and tax-id decision, and must confirmation bind all of those values?
Must the import mapping require and confirm the Customer name, kind and old-reference-to-tax-id decision for every new Customer?

quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest. The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest and the picks the mapping showed, nothing else.

The owner gives each such Customer its kind and its name in the import, as the
  import takes display names (R0-85): a Customer without a name or a kind is
  not a state the record may be in (Primary actions, "record a customer"). The
  owner also says whether the v1 value is the Customer's tax id; one that is
  not is shown in the import's mapping and kept nowhere.
judgement.divergence: One implementation makes the mapping collect, display, validate, and bind every Customer name, kind, and tax-id decision; another obtains or changes those values outside the confirmed mapping, which the owner notices in the imported Customers.
judgement.why: Required Customer transformation decisions are stated, but A16 does not say that confirmation binds them.

topics.topic: Responsibility and measurable requirements for random secret generation
questions: Is random vault generation an external owner obligation, or must Registry verify some property beyond length and inequality?
Is random generation an external owner obligation or a startup condition Registry must somehow verify?
Is vault generation an external operational requirement, or must Registry verify some measurable property beyond byte length and inequality?

quotes: A secret — each token and the owner credential — is at least 32 bytes generated at random by the owner's vault (R0-23); a shorter one fails the start.
No two secrets are equal: two services with one token, or a token equal to the owner credential, fail the start.

serving => checks_passed(config)
for secrets s1 != s2 in config: value(s1) != value(s2) and len >= 32 bytes
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats vault generation as an external owner obligation and checks only length and inequality; another attempts additional entropy or origin validation and refuses configured values, which the owner notices at startup.
judgement.why: The random-vault-generation requirement is not verifiable from the configured secret, and the text does not classify it as external or measurable.

topics.topic: Semantic conditions that make an import record malformed
questions: Which cross-record conditions make an import malformed, including dangling project/customer links, duplicate ids inside the file, duplicate pointer versions, version gaps, multiple published pointers, invalid statuses, missing required facts and inconsistent timestamps?

Which semantic failures make a record malformed, including broken links, duplicate ids inside the file, invalid statuses, nonconsecutive pointer versions, multiple published pointers, missing required values, invalid timestamps and owner-service mismatches?
Which internal inconsistencies make an import record malformed?

quotes: At confirmation Registry checks every conflict again. Any conflict — a project, room or pointer id production holds, a Registry-minted `customer_ref` production holds, a malformed record — refuses the whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).
An import file holding a pointer of an undeclared type is refused as a malformed record (A16).
judgement.divergence: One implementation rejects dangling links, duplicate internal ids, invalid pointer histories, and inconsistent statuses as malformed; another accepts some of them, producing different imported state visible to the owner and callers.
judgement.why: Malformedness is a refusal condition, but only one example is defined and the required cross-record semantic checks are absent.

topics.topic: Sign-in failure counting, lockout, reset, concurrency, and restart semantics
questions: When does the lockout start, do attempts made during lockout count as new refused sign-ins or extend it, does a successful sign-in clear the earlier failures, and does restart clear the counter?
What is the exact state machine for failure counting and lockout, including concurrent attempts and restart?
What are the exact counter, lockout and reset semantics for sign-in throttling?

quotes: After 5 refused sign-ins within 15 minutes, every sign-in — the right credential included — is refused for the next 15 minutes. The count is the instance's, not a caller's: Registry tells no callers apart by address (R0-27).
refused_sign_ins(last 15min) >= 5 => sign_in refused
judgement.divergence: One implementation starts a fixed lockout at the fifth failure, ignores lockout attempts, clears failures on success, and resets on restart; another counts or extends lockout attempts and preserves failures, changing when the owner can sign in.
judgement.why: The lockout start, reset, extension, concurrency, and restart semantics are not defined.

topics.topic: Sort directions, artifact-type ordering, tie-breakers, and embedded-collection ordering
questions: Are all otherwise unspecified name, type, identity and registration-time components ascending, and is type compared by the same Unicode-code-point rule as names?
Do the corresponding list-operation orders apply to every embedded collection, and what orders apply to granted ids and import-preview collections?
What total order is used for artifact types?
What direction applies to every unnamed sort key and identity tie-breaker?

quotes: 'List rooms': by name, then by `room_id` (L10).
'List artifacts': by type, then by version, highest first, then by pointer id (L10).
Names compare by Unicode code point of the stored value; identities compare as their text.

every list answer is totally ordered by its key; equal keys never occur
because each key ends in an identity or a sequence number
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats unspecified keys as ascending Unicode/text order and applies list orders to embedded collections; another chooses descending or storage order, producing differently ordered answers visible to callers.
judgement.why: Several key directions, artifact-type comparison, and embedded-collection orders are not declared.

topics.topic: Whitespace code points and treatment of non-string values in blank-value validation
questions: Which characters count as whitespace for blank-value validation?
Exactly which code points count as whitespace, and how are non-string required and optional values handled by this rule?
Which Unicode characters count as whitespace for the required-value and optional-value rules?

quotes: Field names, types, formal optionality and every answer shape belong to State 6; orders, replay mechanisms, correction semantics and token scopes belong to State 2 (State 0, "Carried to later states"; codex round-01 T5).
judgement.why: The exact whitespace encoding and applicability to non-string field types belong with State 6 field types and validation contracts.

topics.topic: Closed startup configuration schema and required store validation
questions: What exact configuration schema and store conditions are required before serving: reachability, writability, schema version, migrations, integrity and encryption included or excluded?
What is the closed configuration schema and which store connectivity, permissions, schema-version and encryption checks must pass before Registry serves?

quotes: Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).
A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no default to a secret or to the store.
serving => checks_passed(config)
judgement.divergence: One implementation requires a closed schema plus reachable, writable, current, integral, encrypted storage; another accepts extra items or a merely named store and fails later, which operators and callers notice.
judgement.why: A mandatory startup refusal depends on checks_passed, malformed, unknown, and store validity that the texts do not define.

topics.topic: Complete imported and transformed facts shown in the import preview
questions: Which complete set of imported and transformed facts must the owner see before confirming the mapping?
What exact information must the owner see before confirming that the mapping is the one to apply?

quotes:
Field names, types and answer shapes are
States 5 and 6.

What
Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States
5 and 6.
judgement.why: The precise fields and presentation shape of the import preview and imported records belong to the State 6 contract and migration-file schema.

topics.topic: Effect of malformed or conflicting records belonging only to unselected projects
questions: Does a conflicting id belonging only to an unpicked project, room or pointer refuse the import?
Do conflicts or malformed records belonging only to unpicked projects refuse the import?

quotes: Registry reads it as data (A19) and answers the mapping without changing anything: each project the file holds, with its id, status, rooms and pointers; for each project the owner picks, the display name and alias it will arrive under (R0-85); each Customer the import will make and the projects it will link (R0-80); every id that conflicts with one production holds.

At confirmation Registry checks every conflict again. Any conflict — a project, room or pointer id production holds, a Registry-minted `customer_ref` production holds, a malformed record — refuses the whole import, and nothing changes (R0-50, R0-79).
An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers, the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry (M09) in one transaction.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates the entire uploaded file and refuses conflicts or malformation in unpicked projects; another validates only the selected closure and imports successfully, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The validation scope is described as the whole file while the mutation scope is only picked projects, without resolving unpicked failures.

topics.topic: Equivalence of omitted, empty, and whitespace-only optional values during replay comparison
questions: For replay comparison, are an omitted optional fact, an empty string and a whitespace-only string equal or different?
Are an omitted optional value and a supplied blank optional value equal for request-id replay?

quotes: The supplied facts are compared as the caller gave them, value for value; Registry does not normalise them for the comparison. For 'add a room' the project is one of them.
An optional value given as an empty string or white space only is absent.
judgement.why: A01 requires comparison of raw supplied values without normalization, while A02 normalizes every blank optional value to absence.

topics.topic: Number of access-version increments for one action changing multiple access facts
questions: Does one accepted action increment the access version once, or once for every access fact it changes?
Does one accepted action increment the access version once, or once for every access fact it changes?

quotes: A session's access version is 1 at registration and moves by one with each accepted change of its granted set, its active project or its pending request (M06) — a project leaving the set by its erasure included (R0-61).
accepted change of x => version(x)' = version(x) + 1
judgement.divergence: One implementation increments once per accepted action even when it changes several access facts; another increments once per changed fact, so Kernel and stale-version checks observe different versions.
judgement.why: The prose can count changed facts, while the invariant can count the compound action, and no rule resolves the unit of increment.

topics.topic: Ordering of stale-revision, input, lifecycle, and already-in-target-state checks
questions: When more than one condition fails, is revision checked before lifecycle and action-specific preconditions, after them, or according to a declared per-action order?
Are input validation and stale-version checks performed before deciding that a transition is already in its target state?

quotes: A stated revision that is not the record's current one is refused as stale, and nothing changes (R0-35).
An action that would change nothing (A03 rule 4, A05) still states the revision and is refused when it is stale.

A transition to the state a record is already in is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project already in a session's set, making the active project active again, clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered session (R0-53).
A date later than today is refused.
judgement.divergence: One implementation checks malformed input and lifecycle eligibility before staleness and no-op recognition; another checks revision or target state first, returning different refusals or accepting invalid no-op inputs, which the owner notices.
judgement.why: The texts define individual refusals and no-ops but not their precedence when several conditions apply.

topics.topic: Read visibility of pointers whose artifact type was removed
questions: Which read operations remain available for pointers whose type was removed?
Which read projections continue to expose pointers of a removed type?

quotes: A release that removes a type keeps every pointer of it: they stay in the history and are listed and read as before, with their status as it was.
After the removal, publishing that type and 'read the latest artifact of a type' for it are refused as an unknown type, and withdrawing a pointer of it is refused.
judgement.why: The first passage says removed-type pointers remain readable as before, while the second refuses the existing latest-by-type read for that type.

topics.topic: Refusal precedence for agent-authority access and other validation failures
questions: Which refusal takes precedence when a call simultaneously has an unauthorized operation, an unregistered session, a missing or out-of-set project, or an archived project?
Which refusal wins when an agent-authority call fails both the session/project access check and another validation?

quotes: An operation outside a token's row is refused, whatever the request holds.

A call with agent authority is accepted only when the token is Cabinet Kernel's, the session it names is registered, and — for an operation on a project — the project is in that session's set (R0-46, R0-53).

Every refusal of the third check, and of a project that does not exist, is the same answer as for a project that does not exist (R0-47); a call naming an unregistered session is answered as a call outside the set (R0-53).
A write with agent authority on an archived project of the set is refused (R0-12, R0-70); reads of it are answered.
judgement.divergence: One implementation checks token operation rights and access concealment before request, type, lifecycle, and replay validation; another validates those conditions first, returning observably different errors to Kernel.
judgement.why: The required concealment behavior does not establish precedence among authorization and other simultaneous failures.

topics.topic: Registration authorization for a not-yet-registered agent session
questions: How can the registration call succeed when the named session is not registered yet?
How can the registration operation pass A10 when the session being registered does not yet exist?

quotes: A call with agent authority is accepted only when the token is Cabinet Kernel's, the session it names is registered, and — for an operation on a project — the project is in that session's set (R0-46, R0-53).
Cabinet Kernel registers a session when its agent session starts, naming it from its own run context (R0-53, R0-77); registering a registered session answers it unchanged (A05).
Registering the same identity again makes a new session with an empty set.
judgement.why: A10 requires the named session already to be registered for every agent-authority call, while A11 requires registration of a new or ended identity.

topics.topic: Restore-test acceptance criteria, evidence, and release gate
questions: What exact restore test must pass, how is its result recorded, and is release forbidden when it fails?
What constitutes a successful restore test at release time?

quotes: Before each release the owner restores the latest backup into a temporary instance on VM Platform, checks that it starts (A17) and answers, and removes it; a test instance never receives a production backup (R0-34).
judgement.divergence: One release process requires successful integrity checks and representative reads and blocks release on any failure; another treats any startup and single answer as sufficient or proceeds without evidence, which the owner and later callers notice.
judgement.why: Starts and answers does not define the required restored-state checks, evidence, or failure gate.

topics.topic: Whether Cabinet Kernel's token is excluded by the service-token publication ban
questions: Does the prohibition on service tokens exclude Cabinet Kernel's service token when it carries agent authority?
Does "No service token" exclude Cabinet Kernel's agent-authority token, or is A08 rule 2 intended to refer only to document-owner and other non-Kernel services?

quotes: A pointer is published and withdrawn by Cabinet Kernel for the agent, on a project of its session's set (R0-46, A10), or by the owner (R0-88).
No service token has the right to publish or withdraw (A09); a service is refused whatever type it names.

| Cabinet Kernel | with agent authority only (A10): register an agent session; read the session's access; request access to a project; validate a project reference; read the agent projection; list rooms; add a room; list artifacts; read the latest artifact of a type; publish and withdraw an artifact pointer (R0-88) | `business_confidential` (R0-74) |
judgement.why: A08 categorically denies publication rights to service tokens even though Kernel authenticates with such a token and A08 and A09 explicitly grant it publication and withdrawal.

topics.topic: Accepted secret encoding and exact bytes used for length and equality checks
questions: What representation is accepted for secrets and exactly which bytes are counted and compared?

topics.topic: Access-version result when an agent session is ended
questions: Does an accepted end increment a version that is then discarded, return a final version, or merely check the stated version without moving it?

topics.topic: Applicability of concurrent-publish rules to equal versus different request ids
questions: Does A07's two-publish rule apply only when the calls carry different request ids?

topics.topic: Atomicity and conflict handling for concurrent import confirmation and normal creation
questions: What happens when two confirmations run concurrently, or when a normal create introduces a conflicting id between the recheck and the import writes?

topics.topic: Authority of State 1 and State 2 design texts
questions: Which draft provisions are authoritative inputs for later states and code, and are the State 2 decision texts accepted as written or only their underlying proposals?

topics.topic: Calendar and time zone defining today for customer relationship dates
questions: Is the default and upper bound based on UTC, the owner's Europe/Madrid date, or a configured instance zone?

topics.topic: Computation of the import file digest
questions: How is the import file digest computed?

topics.topic: Concurrency semantics for creates sharing a request id
questions: Must equal concurrent calls both succeed with the same record, and must different concurrent calls produce one success and one specified conflict rather than an internal error?

topics.topic: Durable audit-sequence high-water mark after erasure and restart
questions: Where is the last-ever sequence retained after all entries containing it have been erased and the instance restarts?

topics.topic: Fixed catalogue defining security-review completeness
questions: What fixed catalogue determines whether the security review includes every required category?

topics.topic: Measurable encryption and key-management requirements for disks and backups
questions: What measurable encryption and key-management conditions must backups and disks satisfy?

topics.topic: Namespace in which imported identifier conflicts are detected
questions: Does a room id conflict with an existing project or pointer id having the same text, or only with another room id?

topics.topic: Provenance requirements for preserving an imported customer_ref
questions: Can this one VPS import ever preserve a source customer_ref, and if so how does Registry prove that it was Registry-minted rather than merely UUID-shaped?

topics.topic: Recovery of state created or changed after the restored production backup
questions: Are post-backup creations, corrections, grants, request ids, audit sequence numbers and the migration closure intentionally lost, replayed from another log, or required to be recovered by some other mechanism?

topics.topic: Replay of an accepted publication after its artifact type is removed
questions: Does a retry of an already accepted publish still return its pointer after that type has been removed from the release?

topics.topic: Revision semantics of terminal erasure
questions: Does terminal erasure increment a revision before removing it, retain the incremented revision, or consume the stated revision without producing a next revision?

topics.topic: Semantics of granting an already-granted project while also activating it
questions: What happens when the owner grants an already granted project and asks to make it active while another project or none is active?

topics.topic: State used to record owner-session idle activity
questions: What fact records the last owner action needed to enforce the 30-minute idle expiry, and does it mutate on the OwnerSession?

topics.topic: Success and ordering semantics for concurrent audited changes
questions: Must concurrent independently valid changes both succeed with consecutive audit sequence numbers, and what defines their order?

topics.topic: Timestamps recorded for publication and supersession in one transaction
questions: What timestamps are recorded for the two changes made by one publish transaction?

topics.topic: Whether dependency-manifest and digest rules belong to Registry or the external release process
questions: Are A20's dependency manifest and digest verification part of Registry's specification or requirements on an external release process?

topics.topic: Whether pre-release restore testing is a Registry rule or an external release obligation
questions: Is the pre-release restore test a normative Registry State 2 rule or an external release-process obligation outside this case?
